title: Heart Hands Emoji 🫶 Meaning: Love, Thanks and Support
description: The 🫶 heart hands emoji means love, gratitude or support, the way fans shape a heart at a concert. See how it differs from ❤️ and when it reads as platonic.
summary: 🫶 shows two hands curved together into a heart shape. It means love, appreciation or support, and it leans warm and friendly rather than romantic. People send it to say “thank you,” “love you guys,” or “I’m here for you,” copying the hand gesture fans and performers flash at concerts.
meaning: The heart hands emoji is affection with a soft edge. Where a red heart can feel like a declaration, 🫶 feels like something you hold up for a whole room: a thank-you to followers, love for a friend who showed up, appreciation for a kind comment. It is one of the most reliably platonic ways to send love, which is exactly why it caught on so quickly after it reached phones.

The emoji copies a real gesture. Performers, athletes and fans have been forming hearts with their hands for years, at concerts, after goals and in selfies, and the pose was already a fixture of pop and K-pop fan culture before it had an emoji. When Unicode added it in Emoji 14.0 in 2021, people finally had a way to type what they had been doing with their hands in photos.

Younger users treat 🫶 as a sign-off and a reaction as much as a statement. It closes captions (“best night ever 🫶”), answers good news, and softens requests. It also carries a supportive meaning: under a post about a hard day, a breakup or a loss, 🫶 says “sending love” without the weight of words. Brands and creators lean on it for the same reason, since it reads as sincere without being intimate.

It can be romantic, but context has to do the work. From a partner it is sweet and a little playful. From a crush it is ambiguous on purpose, friendlier than ❤️ and warmer than 👍. Because it supports skin tones, many people pick the shade that matches their own hands, which makes it feel more personal than a plain heart.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Between friends, 🫶 mostly means “love you” or “thank you so much” in a low-pressure way. It works after someone does you a favor, checks in on you, or sends a compliment. In group chats it is a quick way to show appreciation for everyone at once, and it rarely gets misread as flirting unless the rest of the conversation already points that way.

contexts.label: On TikTok and Instagram
contexts.body: Creators use 🫶 to thank their audience and to mark wholesome content, and commenters use it to show support without writing a full reply. It appears constantly in fan spaces, especially for music artists, where the hand heart is already part of concert culture. A row of 🫶 under a vulnerable post is the comment-section version of a group hug.

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: A 🫶 from someone you like is a good sign but not a confession. It shows warmth and comfort with you, and people often choose it precisely because it is safer than a red heart. Look at the pattern: if they send it to everyone, it is friendliness; if it shows up alongside late-night replies and inside jokes, it may be more.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: Heart hands is one of the few love-themed emojis that passes in a casual workplace chat. Teams use it to thank a colleague who covered a shift or shipped something difficult. It still signals closeness, so it fits peers you know well better than a first message to a client or a formal note to senior leadership.

examples.text: Thank you for driving me to the airport at 5am 🫶
examples.meaning: Sincere gratitude toward a friend who went out of their way.

examples.text: Happy birthday to my favorite person 🫶
examples.meaning: Affectionate, and could be platonic or romantic depending on the relationship.
Offering quiet support to someone going through a difficult time.
A creator thanking followers for helping them reach a milestone.

examples.text: You didn’t have to do that 🫶
examples.meaning: Touched by an unexpected kind gesture and saying so warmly.
Encouragement after an achievement, with a little extra sparkle.

combos.meaning: Warm appreciation with a glow, common in captions and thank-you posts.
Being moved almost to tears by something kind or wholesome.
Love and solidarity across skin tones, often used for unity or community messages.
Gentle, sincere affection, frequently used for sympathy or support.

confusedWith.difference: ❤️ is the direct symbol of love and often reads as romantic. 🫶 is a gesture someone makes toward you, so it feels more like thanks, support or friendly affection than a statement of being in love.
🫰 is the small Korean finger heart made with one hand, and it doubles as a money or snapping gesture. 🫶 uses both hands to form a full heart and has no money meaning at all.
🤲 shows two open palms side by side, used for prayer, offering or asking. The fingers do not curve into a heart, and its tone is spiritual or pleading rather than affectionate.

avoid: Skip it in formal emails, complaints or any message where warmth could be mistaken for unprofessional familiarity.
Do not use it to reply to serious criticism or an argument, where it can come across as dismissive or sarcastic.
If you want to make romantic intent unmistakable, 🫶 alone is too ambiguous to carry that message.
design: The glyph shows two hands with fingertips touching at the top and thumbs meeting at the bottom, leaving a heart-shaped gap in the middle. Platforms draw it in the default yellow with five skin tone options, and the pose is consistent everywhere; the main variation is how rounded the fingers look and whether a faint outline separates the two hands.

faqs.q: What does 🫶 mean from a girl?
faqs.a: Most often it means appreciation or friendly affection: she is thanking you, supporting you, or showing she enjoys talking to you. It is not automatically romantic. If she pairs it with flirty messages or sends it only to you, it may signal more interest than a casual 🫶 in a group chat.

faqs.q: What does 🫶 mean from a guy?
faqs.a: The same thing it means from anyone: warmth, thanks or support. Guys often use it with close friends and partners because it feels sincere without being heavy. On its own it does not confirm a crush, so read it together with how often and how personally he messages you.

It is platonic by default. People send it to friends, family, followers and coworkers far more than they use it as a declaration of love. It turns romantic only when the relationship or the surrounding words make it so, such as “miss you already 🫶” from someone you are dating.

faqs.q: When did the heart hands emoji come out?
faqs.a: Heart hands was approved in Emoji 14.0 in 2021 and reached most phones over the following year. It was added alongside other hand gestures in the same release, including the finger heart 🫰 and the hand pointing at the viewer 🫵.

faqs.q: Why can’t I see the 🫶 emoji?
faqs.a: Devices that have not been updated since before Emoji 14.0 cannot display it and show an empty box or question mark instead. Updating your operating system or app normally fixes it, and the person you are texting needs a recent version too in order to see it.
